name: Toy presupposition fragment
summary: Sentences are built from the atoms s (there is a king), p, q and a (the king is bald) with not, and, or. A model gives each atom a value true, false or undefined; a is undefined exactly when there is no king. All four theories of this project share this fragment and differ only in the connective tables and the felicity notion.

defs.label: models
defs.text: A model assigns s, p, q a classical value and a any value in V; the auxiliary constraint keeps only models where a is undefined when s is false.

defs.label: connectives
defs.text: not, and, or are interpreted by a truth table fixed by the theory (strong, weak or middle Kleene).

checks.readback: The Python generator enumerates 24 valuations of s, p, q and a, with a ranging over true, false, undefined; the auxiliary principle then removes the 12 where a is defined although there is no king.

notes: Shared by T-SK, T-WK, T-MK and T-MK-some.

name: Consequence and felicity notions
summary: How a discourse is evaluated against the models of the toy fragment: entailment as truth preservation, felicity as definedness. Split from FR-TOY because the felicity notion is what the theories vary (and it could be reused with another object language).

defs.label: entailment
defs.text: The conclusion is true in every model where all premises are true.

defs.label: felicity
defs.text: A predicate on discourses, defined from definedness; the theory chooses every model or some model.

checks.note: Not sure the split from FR-TOY is the right one; kept to show a theory using two fragments.
